text:
sara: Heads-up: saw a tail-latency spike on paged-attn serving yesterday after the allocator change. Investigating kernel chooser flips + KV page fragmentation. attaching short perf log below.

aj: Yikes. Can you paste the small repro or perf snippet?

sara: Quick paste:
```
kernel_choice: flash_variant_batch
seq_len: 1024
batch: 6
kv_pages: 384 (hot: 64)
alloc_policy: slab
lat_p50: 3.9ms
lat_p95: 7.6ms
lat_p99: 23.4ms
kernel_swap_point: after 3 consecutive high-alloc-latencies
```

matt: That p99 looks like fragmentation causing async page faulting + allocator stalls. slab without compaction + many small frees => slow walks.

anita: Did kernel chooser log why it picked flash_variant_batch? We normally prefer fused when batch small and no paging.

sara: chooser log: `chooser_score_fused=0.42, chooser_score_flash=0.67` — flash wins because measured KV residency misses rose. The measured misses spike aligns with compaction sweeps.

zane: Two quick hypotheses: (1) allocator fragmentation increases page table walks, increasing measured 'effective sequence' cost and nudging chooser; (2) batching heuristic treats many inflight short requests as a single large batch after KV page rebinds.

aj: Want a tiny microbenchmark to isolate. I put together this command: 
```
./bench/paged_attn_repro --seq=1024 --batch=6 --kv-pages=384 --kv-hot=64 --alloc=slab --duration=60
```
Outputs reproducible p99 >20ms for me when run on devbox-5.

matt: Try switching to hybrid allocator to see if compaction reduces latency: `--alloc=hybrid`

sara: did that, p99 drops to ~9.8ms, p95 ~5.1ms. Not as low as fused path but much better.

anita: good repro. We should add two telemetry knobs: per-request kernel_choice_reason and allocator_frag_metric (free-run length histogram).

zane: Agreed. Also add a tiny hysteresis in kernel chooser: require flash to win by >0.2 score unless recent 30s avg miss-rate > threshold. Prevent flip-flopping on transient alloc noise.

aj: Also log `kv_page_eviction_count` and `slot_rebalance_count` for the request window. I saw eviction spikes aligned with the p99.

sara: here's a minimal stack trace sample from perf:
```
#0  __alloc_slab_slowpath
#1  slotmap_reclaim_range
#2  kv_page_fault_handler
#3  paged_attn_run
#4  runtime_worker_loop
```

matt: So reclamation happens in hot path -> we must avoid doing full reclaim inside request loop. Consider async reclamation worker + prefetch of KV pages.

anita: For immediate mitigation: (A) flip default alloc policy on Dedicated pools to hybrid for models > 1B, (B) lower kernel chooser sensitivity (alpha) for first 5s after a compaction event, (C) emit a metric we can alert on.

zane: I can make a small PR to kernel chooser with hysteresis today. Will include a feature flag `kernel_chooser_hysteresis_ms`.

aj: I'll add the allocator frag histogram to pager telemetry (bucketed by run-length: [1,2,4,8,16,32,64+]).

sara: Action items:
- zane: PR for chooser hysteresis + flag (ETA end of day)
- aj: telemetry for allocator frag + eviction counts (ETA tomorrow)
- matt: prototype async reclaim worker and benchmark (ETA 2d)
- anita: add canary config to flip Dedicated -> hybrid for models >1B in staging (ETA today)

perf-bot: reminder: deploy of allocator-slab-change rolled out 2026-03-09T20:13Z to hosted-eu (rollout id r-20260309-alloc).

sara: adding one more note: when running microbench with `--trace=kernel_chooser` you can see bursty score deltas right before flip; sample: `score_delta_trace: [+0.02,+0.18,+0.12,+0.25]` where last one crosses threshold.

anita: Can we also try a short-term guard: if `kv_page_eviction_count > 10` in last 1s then pin to fused for next N requests? cheap hack but might kill p99.

zane: ok will add pin-to-fused flag in PR too.

matt: Note for the async reclaim design: remember to keep correct ordering for KV page mapping to avoid races with inflight requests. Use epoch-based reclamation.

aj: I'll run the microbench across the fleet in staging tonight with alloc=hybrid + chooser hysteresis off/on and post results.

sara: thanks all. filing follow-ups in jira: INF-2879 (chooser hysteresis), INF-2880 (alloc frag telemetry), INF-2881 (async reclaim spike-proof).

zane: :thumbsup:

matt: :eyes:

sara: marking this thread resolved for now — will reopen if staging shows regressions after changes.
